questions.q: What is the primary difference between workforce identity and CIAM (Customer Identity and Access Management)?
options: CIAM only applies to Experience Cloud, never to internal employees
Workforce identity never uses SSO, while CIAM always does
There is no meaningful difference; the same design applies to both
Workforce identity deals with a bounded, HR-provisioned population; CIAM deals with a potentially unbounded, often self-registering population
questions.explain: Workforce identity assumes a known, HR-provisioned headcount. CIAM deals with external populations that grow organically through self-service registration, with different risk and experience priorities.

questions.q: Why is requiring a brand-new customer to create and remember a new password often a problem for a public-facing site?
options: It's a conversion killer — added friction discourages signups, which is why self-registration and social sign-on patterns exist
Passwords are more secure than any alternative, so this isn't actually a problem
Customers are legally prohibited from creating passwords
Passwords are technically impossible to implement on Experience Cloud
questions.explain: For customer-facing experiences, reducing registration friction (via social sign-on or streamlined self-registration) is a priority, since every added step risks losing a prospective customer.

questions.q: What does 'progressive profiling' mean in a CIAM context?
options: A synonym for Just-in-Time provisioning
Collecting all of a customer's identity attributes in one long signup form before granting any access
Collecting identity attributes gradually over multiple visits or interactions, rather than all at once
A security technique for detecting bot signups only
questions.explain: Progressive profiling spreads data collection out over time as the relationship deepens, instead of demanding a long registration form up front, reducing initial friction.

questions.q: Why does partner identity sit architecturally between workforce and customer identity?
options: Partners never need any access to Salesforce data
Partner identity is identical to CIAM in every respect
Partners are always treated exactly like employees
Partners are external like customers, but often need persistent role-based access to real business data like employees do, and frequently want delegated administration of their own users
questions.explain: Partners share customers' external/self-registering nature but also share employees' need for ongoing, role-based access to real business processes — and often want their own admin managing their own users.

questions.q: What does 'delegated administration' mean for a partner organization using a Salesforce-backed portal?
options: A partner organization's own designated admin can manage its own users, rather than requiring the host company to manage every individual partner user directly
Partner users automatically get System Administrator profile
It means partners cannot have any admin capabilities at all
The host company's Salesforce admins must personally manage every partner user account
questions.explain: Delegated administration lets a partner's own admin manage their own organization's users, reducing the administrative burden on the host company while still keeping access properly scoped.
